title: Build the Pipeline
instruction: Put the stages in order, from learning to showing.
steps: Learn from past clicks, watches and ratings (offline, before any request)
Retrieve a few hundred candidates out of millions of items
Score and rank each candidate for this user
Re-rank: add diversity, apply business rules, remove what was already seen
Show the final list on screen
why: Models are trained in advance on logged behaviour; nothing is learned while the user waits.
Retrieval is fast and broad: it must not miss good items (high recall), and it can afford to be rough.
Ranking is the precise, expensive model, affordable only because retrieval shrank the list.
The last pass fixes what a pure relevance score gets wrong: five near-identical items, out-of-stock products, things already bought.
The user is waiting: retrieve, rank and re-rank together usually have a budget of a few hundred milliseconds.
debrief: Retrieve, rank, re-rank: each stage trades speed for precision, so the expensive model only ever sees a few hundred items.
